task_3.title: Add built-in CycloneDX SBOM deployers
task_3.description: Version 2.26.0 adds built-in deployers that can emit CycloneDX software bill of materials files directly from the resolved Conan dependency graph. Users can now request CycloneDX 1.4 or 1.6 SBOM output through the deployer mechanism, while the built-in deployers keep the default behavior of not exposing toggles for build or test package inclusion.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users upgrading to 2.26.0 can generate CycloneDX SBOM artifacts through built-in deployers, using supported CycloneDX schema versions and receiving predictable output files for the resolved dependency graph without requiring a custom hook or custom deployer for the common case.

expectation.grounded: Conan must recognize the built-in deployer names `cyclone_1.4.py` and `cyclone_1.6.py`. When either deployer is selected for a graph-based operation, it must call the corresponding `conan.tools.sbom` generator and write a JSON SBOM artifact into the deploy output folder as `sbom-cyclonedx-1.4.json` or `sbom-cyclonedx-1.6.json` respectively. The built-in deployers must keep the default behavior described in the release note: they do not accept deployer-specific options for including skipped build or test packages.
expectation.conceptual: The upgraded release should let users request SBOM generation as a standard deploy step, choosing either CycloneDX 1.4 or 1.6, and receive a JSON SBOM file in the deploy output location that represents the current resolved dependency graph. For the built-in deployers, advanced inclusion controls for build-only or test-only packages are not part of this feature and remain outside the default workflow.

constraints.grounded: Existing built-in deployers must continue to resolve normally alongside the new CycloneDX deployers. The new deployers must emit JSON files with the version-specific filenames above and must rely on the corresponding public SBOM generator entry point for that schema version. The built-in feature must not imply support for passing extra deployer options to alter build-package or test-package omission defaults.
constraints.conceptual: The feature should extend deployment behavior without changing how other deployers are selected or used. Each schema version should produce one clearly named SBOM file, and the built-in option should stay limited to the default SBOM scope rather than introducing new configuration knobs.

behavior: A deployer selection can now target CycloneDX SBOM generation using the built-in names `cyclone_1.4.py` and `cyclone_1.6.py`.
Selecting `cyclone_1.4.py` produces a JSON SBOM file named `sbom-cyclonedx-1.4.json` in the deploy output folder.
Selecting `cyclone_1.6.py` produces a JSON SBOM file named `sbom-cyclonedx-1.6.json` in the deploy output folder.
The generated SBOM content is derived from the current root Conan dependency graph through the matching CycloneDX schema generator.
The built-in CycloneDX deployers do not expose additional options for including skipped build or test packages; those controls remain outside the built-in deployer path.
acceptance_criteria: When a user selects the built-in `cyclone_1.4.py` deployer for a Conan graph operation with an output folder, the operation should create `sbom-cyclonedx-1.4.json` in that deploy output location.
When a user selects the built-in `cyclone_1.6.py` deployer for a Conan graph operation with an output folder, the operation should create `sbom-cyclonedx-1.6.json` in that deploy output location.
When either built-in CycloneDX deployer is used, the produced artifact should be a JSON CycloneDX SBOM representing the resolved graph for the current root package or consumer.
When users rely on the built-in CycloneDX deployers, they should not expect built-in flags or deployer options to switch inclusion of build packages or test packages from the default behavior.
When users continue using existing non-CycloneDX deployers, deployer resolution and behavior should remain unchanged by this addition.

task_1.title: Expose PyEnv virtual environment paths
task_1.description: Conan 2.26.0 extends PyEnv so consumers can directly access the created virtual environment root, its Python executable, and its bin or Scripts directory. The exposed paths are normalized for downstream tooling, while PyEnv command execution and package installation continue to run inside the managed environment.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that PyEnv exposes the managed virtual environment's root directory, Python executable, and executable directory so recipes and external tools can reference the created environment directly.

expectation.grounded: PyEnv should provide public `env_dir`, `env_exe`, and `bin_path` accessors for the virtual environment root, the Python executable inside that environment, and its `bin` or `Scripts` directory. These accessors should return slash-normalized paths, and `generate()`, `run()`, and `install()` should continue to operate against that same PyEnv-managed environment using the exposed executable and bin path.
expectation.conceptual: Users of PyEnv should be able to retrieve the virtual environment location and interpreter path without reconstructing them manually, and those values should be directly usable in build tools and command execution on all supported platforms.

constraints.grounded: The same virtual environment naming and creation flow should remain in place for a given PyEnv configuration, the generated activation script should still be associated with that environment, and PyEnv command execution or pip installation must not fall back to the system Python when the managed environment exists.
constraints.conceptual: The change should add discoverability of the managed environment's paths without changing which environment PyEnv creates or weakening command isolation to that environment.

behavior: `PyEnv.env_dir` returns the root directory of the created virtual environment.
`PyEnv.env_exe` returns the Python executable inside the managed virtual environment.
`PyEnv.bin_path` returns the executable directory for the managed virtual environment, using `Scripts` on Windows and `bin` on other platforms.
The values exposed by `env_dir`, `env_exe`, and `bin_path` use forward-slash path formatting suitable for downstream tool configuration.
`PyEnv.generate()` prepends `bin_path` to `PATH` for the generated environment activation.
`PyEnv.run(args)` executes commands through `env_exe`.
`PyEnv.install(packages, pip_args=None)` invokes pip through `env_exe` so package installation targets the managed virtual environment.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer creates `PyEnv`, it should be able to read `env_dir`, `env_exe`, and `bin_path` and use them to configure external tools without deriving those paths manually.

When these properties are read on Windows, they should identify the virtual environment root, Python executable, and `Scripts` directory using forward slashes; on non-Windows platforms, they should identify the corresponding `bin` directory and interpreter using forward slashes.
When `generate()` is called for a PyEnv instance, the resulting activation environment should place the virtual environment executable directory on `PATH`.
When `run()` or `install()` is used on a PyEnv instance, the executed command should use the interpreter from the managed virtual environment rather than the system interpreter.

task_2.title: Publicly document LocalAPI local workflow contracts
task_2.description: Conan 2.26.0 formally exposes and documents the LocalAPI available through ConanAPI.local. The update clarifies the supported local-development operations for resolving conanfiles, managing editable packages, and invoking source, build, and test flows, including when remotes participate, what is returned, and when a dependency graph is required before execution.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `ConanAPI.local` is treated as an officially supported local-development API and that its contract is clearly defined for conanfile discovery, editable package management, and local `source()`, `build()`, and `test()` execution.

expectation.grounded: `ConanAPI.local` should publicly expose `LocalAPI` as the supported entry point for local workflow helpers. `LocalAPI.get_conanfile_path(path, cwd, py)` should resolve a folder or file input to an absolute Conan recipe path, require a Python recipe when `py=True`, and raise `ConanException` for missing, invalid, or ambiguous recipe selection. `LocalAPI.editable_add(...)` should accept optional `Remote` entries for resolving `python-requires` and return the resulting `RecipeReference`. `LocalAPI.editable_remove(...)` should support removal by path or by declared requirements. `LocalAPI.source(...)` should load the consumer recipe and invoke `source()` without requiring a dependency graph, while `LocalAPI.build(conanfile)` and `LocalAPI.test(conanfile)` should operate only on a `Conanfile` object that already comes from a fully computed and installed dependency graph.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to rely on `ConanAPI.local` as a documented public API for local recipe workflows. The documented contract should explain how recipe paths are resolved, how editable packages are added or removed, when remotes are consulted, what operations return, and which local actions can run directly versus which require a prior install that has already prepared dependencies.

constraints.grounded: Do not alter the existing local workflow semantics while documenting them: `source()` remains graph-independent, `build()` and `test()` continue to require a graph-prepared `Conanfile`, editable automation guidance remains compatible with `WorkspaceAPI`, and conanfile discovery must continue to reject ambiguous or invalid inputs with `ConanException` instead of silently choosing a recipe.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should clarify and stabilize the public contract without changing how existing local workflows behave. It should preserve current failure conditions for invalid recipe selection and keep dependency prerequisites explicit for operations that need an installed graph.

behavior: `ConanAPI.local` is documented as the public API surface for local developer flows such as editable package management and direct local method execution.
When conanfile discovery is requested for a directory, the API resolves to the applicable recipe file and rejects ambiguous directories that contain both supported recipe formats.
When `editable_add()` is used, the operation can use provided remotes to resolve `python-requires` and returns the `RecipeReference` representing the editable package that was registered.
When `editable_remove()` is used, the operation supports removing editables either by local path or by requirement reference.
When `source()` is invoked through `LocalAPI`, it is expected to run without computing a dependency graph.
When `build()` or `test()` is invoked through `LocalAPI`, the passed `Conanfile` is expected to already represent a fully resolved and installed dependency graph.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer uses `ConanAPI.local`, it should be clear from the public API contract that this surface is intended for local development workflows.
When `get_conanfile_path()` is called on a directory containing both `conanfile.py` and `conanfile.txt`, it should fail with `ConanException` rather than selecting one automatically.
When `get_conanfile_path()` is called with `py=True`, it should only accept a Python recipe as valid input.
When `editable_add()` is called with remotes needed for `python-requires`, it should use those remotes and return the resulting `RecipeReference`.
When `source()` is called through `LocalAPI`, it should be documented as runnable without first computing a dependency graph.
When `build()` or `test()` is called through `LocalAPI`, it should be documented as requiring a `Conanfile` produced by a prior dependency-graph computation and installation flow.

task_5.title: Relax `<host_version>` user/channel matching
task_5.description: The upgrade changes Conan's `<host_version>` resolution so build requirements can inherit the version of an existing host dependency without requiring the same user/channel coordinates. This makes host-version tracking work across more package reference combinations while preserving the failure behavior when no host dependency can be resolved.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan resolves `<host_version>` from an existing host dependency even when the corresponding build requirement or tool requirement uses different or omitted user/channel values, while still failing when no matching host dependency exists to provide the version.

expectation.grounded: When a requirement declared with `<host_version>` is resolved against a host dependency already present in the graph, Conan should copy the host dependency version into the requiring reference without enforcing equality of the host dependency's `user` and `channel` against the `<host_version>` reference. The `<host_version>` resolution path should continue to raise `ConanException` when no matching host dependency can be found.
expectation.conceptual: A package that tracks another dependency through `<host_version>` should follow the host package's version based on the dependency relationship, not be blocked just because the package references use different or missing user/channel qualifiers. If there is no corresponding host dependency to follow, resolution should still fail.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the requirement that `<host_version>` must resolve from an existing host dependency in the dependency graph. Preserve the existing failure mode for unresolved host dependencies, and only remove user/channel equality as a rejection condition after a host dependency is located.
constraints.conceptual: The change should broaden valid `<host_version>` matches, not turn missing host dependencies into successful resolutions. Resolution should remain strict about requiring an actual host dependency source for the version.

behavior: A requirement using `<host_version>` now accepts a resolved host dependency even if the host dependency's user/channel differs from the requesting reference's user/channel.
After locating the host dependency, Conan assigns the resolved host dependency version to the `<host_version>` requirement.
If no host dependency is found for the `<host_version>` requirement, Conan still raises a resolution error instead of silently proceeding.
acceptance_criteria: When a package has a host dependency on a reference such as `name/version@user/channel` and a build or tool requirement on `name/<host_version>` or the same reference with different user/channel values, the build or tool requirement should resolve to the host dependency's version rather than failing because of user/channel mismatch.

When a package has a host dependency matching the tracked package name but the `<host_version>` reference omits user/channel while the host dependency includes them, the `<host_version>` requirement should still inherit the host version successfully.
When a package declares a `<host_version>` requirement and no corresponding host dependency exists in the graph, Conan should fail resolution with an error instead of producing a version.

task_4.title: Support important configuration precedence for tool requirements
task_4.description: Conan 2.26.0 adds an explicit `!` priority marker for configuration entries so tool-require `conf_info` values can be treated as higher priority than profile `conf` values during composition, while preserving existing behavior for normal configuration entries.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that configuration values exposed by tool requirements can be marked as explicitly higher priority than profile configuration so consumers receive the tool-provided value when the same `conf` key is defined in both places, without changing the default precedence rules for ordinary `conf` entries.

expectation.grounded: Configuration names accepted by `Conf` and `conf_info` operations must support a trailing `!` marker that designates the entry as important. Important entries must preserve that marker in serialized or dumped configuration output. During `Conf` composition, an incoming important value must override an existing non-important value for the same key, including direct values, list-based append/prepend compositions, dict-based update compositions, and unset or numeric values. This enables tool-requires `conf_info` to take precedence over profile `conf` when the tool-provided entry is marked important.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to mark selected configuration entries as high priority with an explicit `!` suffix. When such an entry comes from a tool requirement, it should win over the same setting coming from profiles, and composed list or dictionary values should reflect that higher priority. Regular configuration entries should continue to behave as before.

constraints.grounded: The `!` marker only changes precedence; it must not change the normalized configuration key itself beyond priority tracking and output representation. Lowercase validation for configuration names must remain in effect. Invalid non-Python `conf` value types must still be rejected. Existing type-safety rules for incompatible compositions must remain enforced, except where important precedence already applies to compatible, numeric, or unset values.
constraints.conceptual: This feature should be an opt-in priority override, not a global change to configuration resolution. Existing validation and error behavior should remain intact, and mismatched configuration types should not be silently coerced.

behavior: A configuration key ending in `!` is interpreted as an important variant of that key and stored under the same base key with elevated priority metadata.
Important configuration entries remain visibly marked as important when configuration is exported, dumped, or serialized.
When an important value is composed onto an existing non-important value for the same key, the important value becomes the effective higher-priority result.

For list-style configuration composition, important entries change the effective ordering so the important contribution is applied ahead of the non-important one instead of following normal precedence.
For dictionary-style update composition, important entries take precedence over non-important dictionaries rather than being merged underneath them.
For scalar, numeric, and unset values, an incoming important entry replaces the previous non-important value for the same key.
If composed values use incompatible types, configuration composition still fails instead of attempting an implicit conversion.
acceptance_criteria: When a tool requirement publishes a `conf_info` entry with a `!` suffix and a profile defines the same `conf` key without `!`, the consumer should observe the tool-provided value as the effective configuration.
When the same configuration key is provided without the `!` suffix, configuration resolution should continue to follow the existing non-important precedence rules.
When important list-based configuration entries are combined with non-important entries of the same key, the resulting list should reflect the important entry in the higher-priority position.

When important dictionary-based configuration entries are combined with non-important entries of the same key, the resulting dictionary should reflect the important entry's priority in the final merged value.
When an important configuration entry is rendered or serialized, the output should preserve the fact that the entry was marked with `!`.
When values for the same configuration key are composed with incompatible types, the operation should still fail rather than silently choosing an arbitrary conversion.

task_6.title: Recipe-level opt-out for virtual env script generation
task_6.description: The upgrade adds a recipe-controlled way to disable automatic generation of virtual environment scripts, so package authors can prevent VirtualBuildEnv and VirtualRunEnv artifacts from being produced when they are not desired.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that recipes can explicitly disable generation of virtual environment scripts so installs do not emit unwanted build or run environment activation artifacts when the recipe opts out.

expectation.grounded: Recipes should be able to declare `virtualbuildenv = False` and/or `virtualrunenv = False` on the ConanFile to disable generation of the corresponding virtual environment scripts during install-time environment setup. When either opt-out is set, the related VirtualBuildEnv or VirtualRunEnv artifacts should not be produced for that recipe.
expectation.conceptual: Package recipes should have a supported way to opt out of automatic build-environment or run-environment script generation. If a recipe disables one of these environment helpers, users should observe that the corresponding environment files are not created.

constraints.grounded: The opt-out should be recipe-driven and scoped to the disabled environment type only. Recipes that do not set these attributes should keep existing behavior, and disabling one virtual environment generator should not require disabling the other.
constraints.conceptual: The new control should be selective, predictable, and backward compatible. Existing recipes should continue to behave the same unless they explicitly opt out, and opting out of one environment script type should not unexpectedly affect unrelated environment generation.

behavior: A Conan recipe can explicitly disable build environment script generation via `virtualbuildenv = False`.
A Conan recipe can explicitly disable run environment script generation via `virtualrunenv = False`.
When a recipe disables a virtual environment type, install-time environment generation omits the corresponding activation and related script outputs for that type.
Disabling both virtual environment types results in no virtual build or run environment scripts being generated for that recipe.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe sets `virtualbuildenv = False` and an install is performed, it should not generate VirtualBuildEnv script artifacts for that recipe.
When a recipe sets `virtualrunenv = False` and an install is performed, it should not generate VirtualRunEnv script artifacts for that recipe.
When a recipe sets both `virtualbuildenv = False` and `virtualrunenv = False`, the install should complete without producing virtual environment script files for either type.
When a recipe does not opt out, virtual environment script generation should remain available with existing behavior.

task_7.title: Add Emscripten compiler detection to detect_api
task_7.description: Conan 2.26.0 adds a dedicated detect API entry point for EMSDK Emscripten compilers. Callers can inspect the default `emcc` executable or a supplied executable name and receive a detected compiler identity and parsed version only when the command output clearly identifies Emscripten; otherwise detection fails safely without producing a false positive.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan exposes a user-facing detect API for EMSDK Emscripten compilers so consumers can identify an `emcc` installation and its compiler version, while safely returning no detection when the executable is missing, unsupported, or not actually Emscripten.

expectation.grounded: Conan 2.26.0 should provide `detect_api.detect_emcc_compiler(compiler_exe="emcc")`. It should invoke the selected executable with `--version`, recognize Emscripten only when the first output line identifies it as Emscripten, extract a semantic version in `major.minor.patch` form, and on success return the tuple `("emcc", Version(parsed_version), compiler_exe)`. If execution fails, the command exits unsuccessfully, the output does not identify Emscripten, no semantic version can be parsed, or another detection-time error occurs, it should return `(None, None, None)`.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to ask Conan’s detect API to inspect the default `emcc` command or a custom executable and get back an Emscripten compiler identity plus version when the tool is genuinely present. If the executable cannot be validated as Emscripten or its version cannot be determined, the API should fail gracefully by reporting no detection instead of raising or misclassifying another compiler.

constraints.grounded: Detection must be specific to Emscripten and must not report success for arbitrary compiler version output. Successful detection is limited to outputs whose first line identifies Emscripten and includes a parseable `major.minor.patch` version. Failure paths should preserve the existing no-detection convention of returning `(None, None, None)`.
constraints.conceptual: The new capability should be conservative: only clear Emscripten installations should be recognized, and ambiguous or failing executions should simply be treated as undetected rather than producing incorrect compiler data.

behavior: A new public detect API entry point is available for Emscripten compiler detection under `detect_api.detect_emcc_compiler`.
By default, the API targets the `emcc` executable, but it also accepts a caller-supplied executable name or path.
The detection routine inspects the executable's version output and treats the first output line as the authoritative identification source.
When that first line identifies Emscripten and contains a semantic version, the API reports compiler id `emcc`, returns the parsed `Version`, and includes the executable that was used.

If the process exits with an error, the output does not identify Emscripten, the version is missing or not parseable as `major.minor.patch`, or detection encounters another runtime error, the API returns no detection as `(None, None, None)`.
acceptance_criteria: When `detect_api.detect_emcc_compiler()` is called against a working `emcc` installation whose version output identifies Emscripten and includes a `major.minor.patch` version, it should return compiler id `emcc`, that parsed version as a `Version`, and the executable name used for detection.

When `detect_api.detect_emcc_compiler(custom_executable)` is called and the custom executable is a valid Emscripten compiler, it should return the same successful detection tuple with the provided executable reflected in the result.
When the inspected executable exits unsuccessfully, it should report no detection by returning `(None, None, None)`.
When the inspected executable's first version-output line does not identify Emscripten, it should report no detection by returning `(None, None, None)`.
When the inspected executable identifies Emscripten but no parseable `major.minor.patch` version is available, it should report no detection by returning `(None, None, None)`.
When detection encounters an execution-time error while probing the executable, it should fail safely and return `(None, None, None)`.

task_9.title: Use filesystem mtimes for cache LRU tracking
task_9.description: Conan 2.26.0 reduces cache maintenance overhead by deriving recipe and package LRU recency from cache folder modification times instead of dedicated database LRU updates, improving warm-cache operations without changing cache compatibility.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Conan 2.26.0 preserves correct least-recently-used tracking for cached recipes and binaries while reducing the overhead of repeated warm-cache operations by using cache folder modification times as the recency signal.

expectation.grounded: PkgCache.get_recipe_lru(ref) should report the recipe cache folder modification time, and PkgCache.get_package_lru(pref) should report the package layout base folder modification time. PkgCache.update_recipes_lru(refs) should refresh recipe recency by updating the corresponding cache folder mtimes, and BinaryInstaller should refresh the package base folder mtime when a binary is reused from BINARY_CACHE. Observable cache recency behavior must no longer depend on reading or writing dedicated database LRU fields.
expectation.conceptual: When Conan reuses recipes or binaries that are already in cache, they should still be treated as recently used, but recency should come from normal filesystem metadata rather than extra database bookkeeping. The upgrade should improve warm-cache performance while preserving visible cache reuse behavior.

constraints.grounded: Recipe and package LRU queries must continue to return comparable recency values based on filesystem timestamps. Package LRU lookup must continue to work for package layouts identified by their base folder, including layouts that may represent a build folder. The upgrade must not require a database migration for legacy LRU columns, and existing caches must remain usable.
constraints.conceptual: Do not regress cache correctness, cache reuse, or compatibility with existing local cache data. Recency tracking should remain available anywhere Conan relies on LRU ordering, and users should not need to rebuild or migrate their cache to benefit from the change.

behavior: Recipe LRU values are derived from the modification time of the recipe cache directory.
Refreshing recipe LRU updates the recipe cache directory modification time instead of persisting a separate database LRU value.
Package LRU values are derived from the modification time of the package layout base folder.
When Conan encounters a binary that is already installed in cache, reusing that binary refreshes the package base folder modification time so it remains recently used.
Warm-cache installs no longer perform the prior bulk package LRU database update pass, reducing cache bookkeeping overhead while preserving recency semantics.
acceptance_criteria: When Conan reads recipe LRU information for a cached recipe, it should reflect that recipe cache directory's current modification time.
When recipe recency is refreshed for cached recipes, subsequent LRU reads should show newer filesystem-based recency values without requiring any database schema migration.
When Conan reads package LRU information for a cached package reference, it should reflect the modification time of that package layout's base folder.

Given a package binary is already present in cache, when Conan reuses it during installation, the package should remain marked as recently used and installation should still proceed as an already-installed cache hit.
During warm-cache graph or install operations, cache recency tracking should remain correct while avoiding the extra dedicated package LRU database update overhead from earlier versions.

task_10.title: Expose author metadata in ConanFileInterface
task_10.description: The upgrade adds support for reading a recipe author's metadata through Conan's ConanFileInterface. Consumers that inspect recipe metadata through this interface can now access the author value directly, aligned with other exposed metadata fields.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users and integrations reading recipe metadata through ConanFileInterface can access the recipe's author information as a supported interface attribute.

expectation.grounded: ConanFileInterface must expose an `author` attribute as a readable property. Reading `ConanFileInterface.author` must surface the same value held by the underlying ConanFile `author` attribute, in the same way other metadata properties such as `description` and `homepage` are exposed.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to retrieve a recipe's author metadata from the standard Conan file interface without reaching into lower-level objects or custom workarounds.

constraints.grounded: The new behavior must be limited to making `author` available on ConanFileInterface. Accessing `author` should behave as a direct metadata read and should not alter existing metadata access patterns or the values returned by other interface properties.
constraints.conceptual: The change should simply expand the available metadata on the public-facing interface, without changing how existing metadata fields behave.

behavior: ConanFileInterface includes a readable `author` property.
Reading `ConanFileInterface.author` returns the underlying recipe author's value without additional transformation.
Metadata consumers can obtain author information from the interface layer alongside other already exposed recipe metadata.
acceptance_criteria: When a recipe defines author metadata, accessing it through ConanFileInterface should return that author value.
When code inspects recipe metadata through ConanFileInterface, author should be available as a first-class interface attribute.
When existing consumers read other metadata properties from ConanFileInterface, their behavior should remain unchanged by the addition of author access.

task_8.title: Harden generated environment scripts for unset variables
task_8.description: Conan 2.26.0 changes generated shell environment scripts so prepend and append operations account for missing prior environment-variable values. This hardens generated .sh and PowerShell activation scripts and prevents malformed leading or trailing separators when the existing variable is unset or empty.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that generated environment activation scripts handle prepend and append operations safely when the target environment variable does not already have a usable value, so scripts do not fail in hardened shells and do not produce extra separators around empty values.

expectation.grounded: EnvVars.save_sh() should generate .sh exports that conditionally include the current variable reference only when that variable already has a value, for both path-style and generic separator-based variables. EnvVars.save_ps1() should likewise generate conditional assignment when the rendered value depends on $env:NAME, so the previous environment value is preserved only when present and omitted otherwise.
expectation.conceptual: Generated activation scripts should adapt to whether an environment variable already has a value. When a prior value exists, prepend and append behavior should preserve it with the correct separator; when no prior value exists, the script should set only the new content without malformed separators or shell failures.

constraints.grounded: Direct assignments that do not depend on the previous variable value must continue to be emitted as normal assignments. Empty EnvVars entries must continue to remove the target variable. Separator handling must remain consistent with the variable kind, using the configured path separator for path variables and the configured generic separator otherwise.
constraints.conceptual: Ordinary set and unset behavior should remain unchanged. Only cases that combine new content with an existing variable value should receive the new conditional handling, and separator rules must stay consistent with the variable's normal formatting.

behavior: Generated .sh scripts must avoid expanding an unset existing variable during prepend or append operations by using conditional inclusion of the prior value.
When a generated .sh script prepends to a variable and the variable is unset or empty, the resulting value must contain only the new prefix content without a trailing separator.
When a generated .sh script appends to a variable and the variable is unset or empty, the resulting value must contain only the new suffix content without a leading separator.
When the target variable already has a value, generated .sh prepend and append operations must preserve that value and insert exactly one configured separator between the old and new segments.

Generated .ps1 scripts must branch when the computed assignment depends on the current $env:NAME value, using the combined value only when a current value exists and otherwise assigning the new content alone.
acceptance_criteria: Given a generated .sh activation script that prepends to a path-like variable, when the variable is unset and the script is sourced in a strict shell, it should succeed and set the variable to only the new segment.

Given a generated .sh activation script that prepends to a variable with an existing value, when the script is sourced, it should preserve the prior value and insert one separator between the new and existing segments.
Given a generated .sh activation script that appends to a variable, when the target variable is unset or empty, it should assign only the appended content and should not emit a leading separator.

Given a generated .sh activation script that appends to a variable with an existing value, when the script is sourced, it should retain the original value and add the new content with exactly one separator.

Given a generated PowerShell activation script whose assignment references the current environment variable, when the variable has no current value it should assign only the new content, and when the variable already has a value it should preserve that value with exactly one separator and no empty leading or trailing separator.

task_11.title: Add opt-in rpath-link support for Conan CMake and Meson toolchains
task_11.description: Conan 2.26.0 adds an opt-in build configuration for generated CMake and Meson toolchains to pass link-time search paths for host dependency library directories. This is intended to prevent GNU linker failures, especially in sysroot or cross-build scenarios where transitive shared libraries are needed during linking but should not be relied on through rewritten runtime rpath handling alone.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan-generated CMake and Meson builds can opt in to supplying link-time search paths for transitive shared libraries from host dependencies, particularly when building with a non-root sysroot, so executables and related link steps can resolve indirect shared-library dependencies without depending only on runtime rpath behavior.

expectation.grounded: Expose a built-in `tools.build:add_rpath_link` configuration that Conan 2.26.0 honors in CMake and Meson toolchains. When enabled, `CMakeToolchain` must add `-rpath-link` entries for all host dependency library directories to generated executable and shared linker flags, and `MesonToolchain` must add the corresponding `-rpath-link` entry to generated linker flags. `CMakeToolchain` must also allow the behavior to be enabled through its public `add_rpath_link` attribute. The additional search paths must be derived from host requirements' aggregated `cpp_info.libdirs` and omitted when the feature is disabled or no such directories exist.
expectation.conceptual: Users upgrading to Conan 2.26.0 should be able to turn on a single option that makes Conan-generated CMake and Meson builds pass link-time shared-library lookup paths for host dependencies. With that option enabled, cross-builds and sysroot-based builds should be able to link against transitive or private shared libraries that the GNU linker needs to see at link time, without changing default behavior for users who do not opt in.

constraints.grounded: The behavior must remain opt-in. It must only contribute library directories from non-build requirements, and it must not add extra linker flags when disabled or when host dependencies do not expose library directories. For CMake, both the global configuration and the `CMakeToolchain.add_rpath_link` attribute may enable the behavior; for Meson, the global configuration must control it.
constraints.conceptual: The new behavior should be narrowly scoped to Conan's generated CMake and Meson toolchains and should only affect builds that explicitly request it. It should not change unrelated dependency resolution rules, pull in build-tool dependencies, or alter default linking behavior for existing projects that do not enable the feature.

behavior: Conan registers a new built-in configuration key, `tools.build:add_rpath_link`, for generated CMake and Meson toolchains.
When `tools.build:add_rpath_link` is enabled, Conan-generated CMake toolchains append `-rpath-link` search paths for host dependency library directories to both executable and shared linker flags.
CMake toolchain generation also exposes a public `add_rpath_link` switch that can enable the same behavior without relying only on the global configuration.
When `tools.build:add_rpath_link` is enabled, Conan-generated Meson toolchains append an `-rpath-link` linker flag built from host dependency library directories.
Only host requirements contribute library directories to this feature; build requirements are excluded.
If the feature is not enabled, or if host dependencies expose no library directories, Conan emits no additional `-rpath-link` flags.
acceptance_criteria: When a project uses Conan 2.26.0 with generated `CMakeToolchain` output and enables `tools.build:add_rpath_link`, the generated linker configuration should include link-time `-rpath-link` search paths for the library directories of host dependencies.
When a project enables `CMakeToolchain.add_rpath_link`, the generated CMake linker configuration should behave as if the opt-in setting were enabled globally for this feature.

When a project uses Conan 2.26.0 with generated `MesonToolchain` output and enables `tools.build:add_rpath_link`, the generated Meson linker flags should include a link-time `-rpath-link` entry covering host dependency library directories.

When the build uses a non-root sysroot and depends on transitive shared libraries from host dependencies, enabling this feature should allow the generated toolchain to expose those library locations to the linker during the link step.
When the feature is disabled, generated CMake and Meson toolchains should not add any new `-rpath-link` flags because of this upgrade.
When dependencies are build-only requirements or do not publish library directories, they should not contribute `-rpath-link` search paths through this feature.

task_12.title: Support case-only CMake package name variants in CMakeConfigDeps
task_12.description: Conan 2.26.0 extends CMakeConfigDeps so packages can declare additional casing variants of their CMake package name for consumer find_package calls. The generator now exposes those accepted variants consistently, while rejecting invalid aliases and warning when package-defined variants conflict with an explicit consumer-selected CMake package name.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CMakeConfigDeps lets packages expose additional case-only CMake package name variants so consumers can call find_package with supported capitalization variants, and ensure that invalid or conflicting variant declarations are handled predictably.

expectation.grounded: When a package defines the `cmake_file_name_variants` property, `CMakeConfigDeps` should treat the canonical `cmake_file_name` and each accepted variant as equivalent names for generated package discovery paths, so consumers may use any declared casing with `find_package`. Accepted variants must represent the same name differing only in upper/lower case. If variants introduce a different normalized name and no explicit `cmake_file_name` override exists, generation should fail with `ConanException`. If an explicit `cmake_file_name` is defined and package-provided variants do not match it case-insensitively, generation should continue using only the explicit name and emit a warning.
expectation.conceptual: Packages should be able to advertise approved capitalization variants of the same CMake package name, and consumers should be able to resolve the package with any of those variants. Configuration that changes the package name rather than its casing should not be silently accepted; it should either fail clearly or be ignored with a warning when an explicit package name override already controls lookup.

constraints.grounded: Only case-only variants of a single normalized package name are supported. Declaring multiple variants that normalize to different names is invalid. Package-defined variants must not override an explicit `cmake_file_name` selected for the dependency by the consumer. Existing canonical `cmake_file_name` behavior must remain available even when no variants are declared.
constraints.conceptual: This feature is limited to capitalization aliases, not arbitrary alternate names. A user-selected package name remains authoritative, and the new behavior must preserve existing package discovery for the canonical name.

behavior: `CMakeConfigDeps` accepts a `cmake_file_name_variants` list and exposes the same package discovery directory for the canonical CMake package name and each accepted case-only variant.
When package discovery uses generated config files, all accepted variants resolve to the generated dependency location rather than only the default casing.
When `cmake_find_mode` disables generated config output and Conan discovers an existing package config location, that discovered location is associated with every accepted package-name variant.
When multiple `cmake_file_name_variants` entries differ by more than case, generation fails with `ConanException` instead of accepting multiple distinct names.
When package-provided variants differ from the dependency's effective `cmake_file_name` by more than case and no explicit override exists, generation fails with `ConanException`.

When an explicit `cmake_file_name` override is in effect and package-provided variants do not match that override by case alone, Conan warns and ignores the variants rather than generating alias entries for them.
acceptance_criteria: When a package declares one or more `cmake_file_name_variants` that differ from its effective CMake package name only by capitalization, consumers using `CMakeConfigDeps` should be able to resolve that dependency with `find_package` using any declared variant.
When no `cmake_file_name_variants` are declared, CMake package discovery behavior should remain unchanged for the canonical package name.
When `cmake_file_name_variants` contains entries that normalize to different names, dependency generation should fail with `ConanException` rather than generating multiple unrelated package aliases.

When a dependency has an explicit `cmake_file_name` override and package-provided variants do not match that override by case alone, generation should keep the explicit package name as the only supported name and should emit a warning.
When package discovery relies on an existing package config location instead of generated config files, each accepted case-only variant should still resolve to that same package location.

task_14.title: Support ABI-sensitive dependency options in consumer package IDs
task_14.description: Conan 2.26.0 adds a recipe-level way for dependencies to declare option values, such as `shared`, that must participate in downstream consumer package ID calculation when header-driven ABI differences can change produced binaries, including non-embed cases.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan recipes can declare dependency options that must affect a consumer's `package_id` when dependency headers can change the consumer binary ABI, including non-embed relationships.

expectation.grounded: Provide support for a recipe attribute named `package_id_abi_options` so a dependency can list option names whose current values must be incorporated into the consumer `package_id`. This contribution must apply when the consumer `package_type` is `application`, `shared-library`, or `static-library`, and only for dependencies whose headers are part of the consumer graph. Header-propagated transitive dependencies must also affect the consumer `package_id` through the same mechanism. If the attribute is absent, no additional dependency options should be injected into the consumer `package_id` by this feature.
expectation.conceptual: Consumers that build binary artifacts should get distinct package IDs when a dependency explicitly marks ABI-relevant options and those dependency headers can alter the consumer binary. This should work even when the dependency is not embedded, and it should also apply through transitive header exposure. Dependencies that do not opt in, or whose headers do not reach the consumer, should not change the consumer package ID through this feature.

constraints.grounded: Only option names explicitly listed in a dependency's `package_id_abi_options` may affect downstream consumer `package_id` values through this mechanism. The effect is limited to consumer package types `application`, `shared-library`, and `static-library`, and to dependency edges marked as providing headers. Dependencies without propagated headers, or without the attribute in the active configuration, must leave this feature inactive. Existing package ID behavior for other dependency relationships must remain intact.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the scope narrow: only explicitly opted-in ABI-sensitive dependency options should alter downstream binary identity, and only when those dependency headers can actually affect the consumer artifact. Consumers outside binary-producing package types, or dependency relationships without header influence, should behave as before.

behavior: A dependency recipe can declare `package_id_abi_options` to identify which of its option values are ABI-relevant for downstream consumers.
For consumers with package types `application`, `shared-library`, or `static-library`, changing an opted-in option value on a header-providing dependency changes the consumer `package_id`.
The same package ID influence applies to transitive dependencies when their headers are propagated to the consumer through the dependency graph.
Dependencies that do not provide headers to the consumer do not affect the consumer `package_id` through `package_id_abi_options`.
If a dependency does not define `package_id_abi_options` for the active configuration, this feature adds no extra package ID variability for that dependency.
acceptance_criteria: When a dependency declares `package_id_abi_options` and a binary-producing consumer uses that dependency's headers, changing one of the declared option values should produce a different consumer package ID.
When the same dependency relationship does not expose headers to the consumer, changing a declared ABI option should not change the consumer package ID through this feature.

When a transitive dependency's headers are propagated to a binary-producing consumer and that dependency declares `package_id_abi_options`, changing a declared option value should change the consumer package ID.
When a dependency does not declare `package_id_abi_options` in the active configuration, changing its options should not alter the consumer package ID through this new mechanism.
When the consumer is not an `application`, `shared-library`, or `static-library`, this feature should not introduce additional dependency-option-driven package ID changes.

task_13.title: Add function-style deactivation support for Windows batch env scripts
task_13.description: Conan 2.26.0 extends `tools.env:deactivation_mode=function` to generated Windows `.bat` environment scripts so Windows command prompt workflows can activate Conan environments and later deactivate them with clean restoration of prior environment state, including aggregated activation scripts.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Windows users who enable `tools.env:deactivation_mode=function` can use Conan-generated `.bat` environment scripts with the same function-style activation and deactivation workflow available for shell and PowerShell scripts, including correct restoration or removal of environment variables after deactivation.

expectation.grounded: When `tools.env:deactivation_mode=function` is enabled, Conan-generated batch scripts produced from `EnvVars.save_bat()` and aggregated environment launchers produced from `generate_aggregated_env()` must expose a callable `deactivate_<name>` batch command in the active `cmd.exe` session. Calling that deactivation command must restore each captured environment variable to its previous value, or clear it if it was not previously defined. Aggregated batch launchers such as `conanbuild.bat` must activate their component scripts and provide a matching group deactivation command that deactivates the included scripts. In this mode, Conan must not emit the standalone vcvars batch deactivation file because Visual Studio vcvars deactivation is not supported through that path.
expectation.conceptual: With function-style deactivation enabled, Windows command prompt users should be able to activate a Conan environment and then deactivate it from the same session through a generated deactivation command, with the shell state returning to what it was before activation. This should work both for individual environment scripts and for aggregated Conan activation scripts.

constraints.grounded: When `tools.env:deactivation_mode` is not set to `function`, the existing file-based `.bat` activation and `deactivate_*.bat` generation behavior must remain unchanged. Function-mode deactivation must clean up its temporary command exposure and not leave stale helper PATH entries or scope-tracking state after deactivation. The Windows change must preserve the existing aggregated `.sh` and `.ps1` function-mode contract.
constraints.conceptual: Default upgrade behavior must remain backward compatible, and the new Windows function-mode support must not leave residual helper state behind after deactivation. The feature should align Windows behavior with the established cross-shell activation/deactivation model rather than introducing a separate contract.

behavior: Enabling `tools.env:deactivation_mode=function` causes Conan-generated Windows `.bat` environment activators to provide a matching deactivation command in the current command prompt session instead of relying only on a sibling deactivate file.
The generated batch deactivation flow restores modified variables to their prior values and removes variables that were introduced by activation when those variables were previously undefined.
Aggregated batch activators such as `conanbuild.bat` create a single matching deactivation command that deactivates the aggregated component scripts and restores the overall session environment.

Function-mode batch activation and deactivation clean up the temporary helper location used to expose the deactivation command so repeated activate/deactivate cycles do not accumulate stale PATH entries.
When Visual Studio vcvars participates in a function-mode batch activation flow, Conan does not generate a standalone batch deactivation script for vcvars.
acceptance_criteria: Given Windows `cmd.exe` and `tools.env:deactivation_mode=function`, when a user calls a Conan-generated environment `.bat` activation script, a corresponding `deactivate_<script>` command should become callable in that same session.

When the user invokes the generated deactivation command, every environment variable changed by activation should return to its previous value, and variables that did not exist before activation should be unset.

Given an aggregated Conan batch activator such as `conanbuild.bat`, when it activates multiple environment scripts, invoking its matching deactivation command should reverse the aggregated environment changes from one command.

When activation and deactivation are repeated in the same Windows session with function mode enabled, the workflow should continue to work without leaving stale helper PATH entries or requiring manual cleanup.
Given the default non-function deactivation mode, Conan should continue to generate and use the existing file-based `.bat` deactivation workflow.

task_15.title: Add explicit cache signing and verification for packages
task_15.description: Conan 2.26.0 introduces explicit `conan cache sign` and `conan cache verify` workflows for package signing, standardizes the metadata written for signed artifacts, verifies artifact checksums during signature verification, and removes implicit signing from the upload flow in favor of a separate pre-upload signing step.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that package signing and verification can be performed explicitly from the local cache, that signed recipes and packages expose standardized signature metadata, and that users receive clear per-item errors when integrity or signature validation fails instead of relying on implicit signing during upload.

expectation.grounded: Conan must provide `conan cache sign` and `conan cache verify` subcommands that operate on selected cache recipes and packages from either a reference pattern or a package list, with optional `--package-query` filtering. `conan cache sign` must require the package-sign plugin `sign()` hook, create standardized `pkgsign-manifest.json` and `pkgsign-signatures.json` metadata for each signed recipe or package, and surface per-item `pkgsign_error` results while still processing the full selection. The manifest must describe artifact files with SHA-256 digests, and the signatures metadata must capture the plugin-reported signing method, provider, and signed artifact mapping. `conan cache verify` must require the plugin `verify()` hook, validate artifact checksums against the manifest before invoking plugin verification when the manifest exists, and report item-level verification failures through command results and overall command error status. If a legacy plugin `sign()` does not return the standardized signatures structure, or signed content lacks the manifest, Conan should emit a deprecation warning. The `upload` command must no longer perform implicit signing and should instead warn users to run `conan cache sign` before uploading when signing is configured.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to explicitly sign and verify cached packages and recipes before distribution, with a consistent metadata format that describes what was signed and how it was signed. Verification should check both artifact integrity and plugin-defined signature rules, report failures per affected item, and treat signing as a separate step from upload. Older signing plugins may still run temporarily, but users should be warned when they do not provide the new metadata expected by the upgraded workflow.

constraints.grounded: The new signing flow must remain explicit: `upload` must not silently sign artifacts. `conan cache sign` and `conan cache verify` must reject missing target selection, mutually exclusive simultaneous pattern and list input, and empty resolved package lists. Verification must hash only actual artifact files, exclude metadata entries from the verification file set, and tolerate manifests that omit optional absent artifacts by checking cache files against manifest entries rather than requiring every manifest entry to exist locally. Missing plugin hooks must raise configuration errors for the corresponding command instead of silently succeeding.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must not hide signing work inside unrelated commands, must fail clearly when users provide invalid or empty target selections, and must keep integrity checks focused on real distributable artifacts rather than internal metadata. Verification should be strict about changed files, but compatible with older signed content through warnings instead of silent false success.

behavior: `conan cache sign` signs selected recipes and packages in the local cache using either a reference pattern or an explicit package list, and supports additional package filtering.

Signing now prepares cache artifacts for the selected items even outside the upload flow, and command results preserve per-recipe or per-package signing errors instead of aborting at the first failure.
Before plugin signing runs, Conan generates a standardized manifest JSON for each recipe or package that lists artifact filenames and their SHA-256 checksums in deterministic order.

When the plugin `sign()` hook returns signature descriptors, Conan persists them in a standardized signatures metadata JSON; each descriptor must include a signing method, a signing provider, and a mapping of signed artifacts.
If the plugin `sign()` hook follows the legacy contract and does not return the standardized signatures list, Conan emits a deprecation warning rather than failing immediately.

`conan cache verify` loads selected cache recipes and packages, recomputes artifact checksums against the stored manifest when present, and only then invokes the plugin `verify()` hook for signature-specific validation.
A checksum mismatch during verification is treated as a signing verification error for the affected recipe or package and is surfaced in the command results.
If the standardized manifest is missing, Conan emits a deprecation warning and skips checksum verification instead of fabricating checksum results.
The text formatter for cache sign and cache verify reports processed items plus an OK/FAILED summary, and the command returns an overall error when any selected item records a package-signing error.
Uploading no longer triggers implicit package signing; when a signing plugin is configured, upload warns that users must run `conan cache sign` before upload.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs `conan cache sign` with a valid target selection and a configured signing plugin, Conan should process the selected cache recipes and packages and return structured results for all processed items rather than only the first one encountered.

When signing completes under the new plugin contract, each signed recipe or package should expose standardized manifest and signatures metadata describing the signed artifact files, their digests, and the signing method/provider information.

When a user runs `conan cache verify` for previously signed cache content, Conan should validate artifact integrity against stored digests before plugin verification and should fail the affected item if any artifact checksum does not match.

When verification encounters signed content produced by an older plugin that does not provide the standardized manifest, Conan should warn that the metadata is deprecated and continue with plugin-level verification without checksum validation.
When the required `sign()` or `verify()` plugin hook is not configured, the corresponding cache command should fail with a configuration error instead of pretending to succeed.
When a user provides no selection, both a pattern and a package list, or a selection that resolves to no packages, the cache sign or verify command should fail clearly instead of doing nothing.
When any selected recipe or package fails to sign or verify, the command should still report all processed items, mark the failing ones in the results, and exit with an overall Conan error status.
When a user uploads packages after this upgrade, upload should not perform signing itself and should direct users toward the explicit cache-signing workflow if signing is configured.

task_17.title: Restore legacy CMakeConfigDeps definitions formatting
task_17.description: Conan 2.26.0 fixes the legacy definitions output generated by CMakeConfigDeps so package definition variables are emitted in a CMake-friendly format again. This restores direct compatibility with older CMake consumption patterns that pass generated definitions to commands such as add_definitions and try_compile-style argument lists, including definitions that contain assigned values.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to Conan 2.26.0 restores legacy CMakeConfigDeps compatibility by generating package definition variables in a format that downstream CMake projects can pass directly to legacy definition-consuming APIs, including definitions with assigned values.

expectation.grounded: When CMakeConfigDeps generates legacy package variables from dependency cpp_info.defines, the generated <package>_DEFINITIONS value should expose each definition as its own -D-prefixed CMake list entry, preserving define order and supporting both plain macro names and NAME=value forms. The generated value should remain consumable as a CMake list so it can be forwarded directly to legacy APIs such as add_definitions and try_compile-related arguments.
expectation.conceptual: Generated dependency definition variables should behave like ready-to-use CMake compile-definition arguments. Consumers should be able to reuse them directly in older CMake integration flows without manually adding -D prefixes, splitting strings, or repairing definitions that include values.

constraints.grounded: The fix must be limited to the observable format and escaping of the legacy CMakeConfigDeps *_DEFINITIONS variable. Definitions must still come from the package's declared cpp_info.defines, and existing target names, library variables, and include directory handling must not regress as part of this change.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should correct malformed legacy definition output without changing the source of package metadata or altering unrelated CMake dependency information.

behavior: CMakeConfigDeps now emits legacy <package>_DEFINITIONS values as a semicolon-delimited CMake list of -D-prefixed entries instead of a space-joined raw define string.
Each declared definition is represented as an individual list element, so multiple definitions remain separable and reusable by CMake consumers.
Definitions that include assigned values, such as NAME=value, are preserved as single definition entries and escaped for safe CMake consumption.
The generated legacy definitions variable can be passed directly to older CMake commands that expect compile-definition arguments.
acceptance_criteria: Given a dependency that declares a single define through cpp_info.defines, when CMakeConfigDeps generates its config files, the generated legacy definitions variable should expose one -D-prefixed definition entry.

Given a dependency that declares multiple defines including an assigned-value define such as NAME=value, when CMakeConfigDeps generates its config files, the generated legacy definitions variable should expose distinct list entries for each definition without losing the assigned value form.

When a consumer forwards the generated legacy definitions variable to CMake commands such as add_definitions or try_compile-style argument lists, the definitions should be consumable directly without manual string rewriting.
Upgrading to Conan 2.26.0 should restore legacy CMakeConfigDeps definition handling while leaving unrelated generated dependency metadata behavior unchanged.

task_16.title: Fix PyInstaller Conan system tools packaging and env script behavior
task_16.description: Conan 2.26.0 fixes a circular-import-driven packaging issue that could omit conan.tools.system from PyInstaller-built standalone binaries, causing runtime failures for recipes that use system package manager helpers. The update also refines generated environment activation and deactivation scripts so grouped shell scripts, function-based deactivation, and variables that were previously unset behave consistently across Windows, PowerShell, and POSIX shells.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan standalone binaries built with PyInstaller can use recipes that rely on `conan.tools.system.package_manager` without missing-module failures, and ensure that generated environment activation/deactivation scripts correctly handle function-based deactivation and previously unset variables across supported shells.

expectation.grounded: When Conan runs from a PyInstaller-built standalone binary, importing or using `conan.tools.system` and `conan.tools.system.package_manager` must remain available at runtime instead of failing because the module was not bundled. Conan's generated environment scripts from `EnvVars` and the aggregated `conan<group>.bat`, `conan<group>.ps1`, and `conan<group>.sh` launchers must keep generator-relative path resolution working, expose group-level deactivate entrypoints when `tools.env:deactivation_mode=function`, and avoid leaving unresolved `%VAR%` or `$VAR` placeholders or extra separators when a target environment variable did not previously exist.
expectation.conceptual: A packaged Conan executable should behave like a normal install for recipes that use system package manager tooling. Its generated environment scripts should activate and deactivate cleanly, including when deactivation is exposed as callable shell functions and when affected environment variables start out unset.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress normal non-PyInstaller Conan usage or existing environment generation for build/run groups. Aggregated environment scripts must still be generated per group for `.bat`, `.ps1`, and `.sh`; standalone deactivate files should continue to exist when function deactivation is not enabled; and deactivation in function mode must restore prior values without leaving temporary PATH entries, dangling separators, or stale scope-tracking variables behind.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must preserve existing environment generator workflows while making packaged binaries reliable. Activation and deactivation must remain reversible, shell-appropriate, and free of leftover state or malformed variable values.

behavior: PyInstaller-built standalone Conan binaries now keep `conan.tools.system` available so recipes using `conan.tools.system.package_manager` do not fail at runtime due to a missing bundled module.
Aggregated environment generation is invoked without eagerly importing the full environment module graph, preventing the import cycle that previously interfered with PyInstaller module collection.

When `tools.env:deactivation_mode=function` is enabled, aggregated `.sh` and `.ps1` environment scripts expose a group-level deactivate function that runs the corresponding per-script deactivation routines in reverse order and then removes itself.

When `tools.env:deactivation_mode=function` is enabled on Windows, generated `.bat` activation scripts create and use a scope-specific temporary location for deactivation commands, add it to `PATH`, and generated deactivation removes that temporary path and clears the bookkeeping variable.

Generated Windows `.bat` activation scripts now distinguish between variables that already exist and variables that are unset, so activating an environment initializes unset variables without preserving literal self-references.
Generated POSIX `.sh` activation scripts now avoid introducing redundant path or list separators when prepending or appending values to a variable that was previously unset.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Conan executable bundled with PyInstaller, when a recipe imports or uses `conan.tools.system.package_manager`, it should execute without a `ModuleNotFoundError` caused by `conan.tools.system` being absent from the bundle.

When Conan generates aggregated environment launchers for a group and `tools.env:deactivation_mode=function` is enabled, sourcing or calling the generated script should make a matching group-level deactivate command available for that shell.

When a generated activation script prepends or appends to an environment variable that was previously unset, activating it should produce a valid final value without leaving literal variable placeholders or empty separators in the environment.

When a Windows function-based environment script is deactivated, it should restore prior values and remove the temporary deactivation directory from `PATH` so no scope-specific cleanup state remains active.
When function-based deactivation is not enabled, Conan should continue to emit the usual standalone deactivation scripts alongside aggregated activation scripts.

task_18.title: Expose .txz and .tzst support in conan cache save help
task_18.description: The upgrade corrects the user-facing help for `conan cache save --file` so it reflects all supported archive extensions, keeps `.tgz` documented, and makes the limitations of `.txz` and `.tzst` visible to users before they choose an output format.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan cache save` clearly communicates the supported output archive formats for `--file`, including the availability of `.txz` and `.tzst`, the experimental status of those formats, and the Python version requirement for `.tzst`.

expectation.grounded: The `conan cache save` CLI help for the `--file` option should describe the argument as saving to a file rather than only a `.tgz` file, and it should list `.tgz`, `.txz`, and `.tzst` as allowed extensions. The help text should also indicate that `.txz` and `.tzst` are experimental and that `.tzst` requires Python 3.14 or newer.
expectation.conceptual: Users invoking help for `conan cache save` should see an accurate description of which archive formats they can request for `--file`, along with any format maturity or runtime-version limitation that affects whether a format can be used.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress the documented support for `.tgz`. The exposed contract for `--file` should not imply unconditional `.tzst` availability on Python versions below 3.14, and the help output should preserve the distinction that `.txz` and `.tzst` are experimental formats.
constraints.conceptual: The command documentation should remain backward compatible for existing archive usage, avoid overstating support in unsupported environments, and present format limitations clearly enough that users can choose a valid output format.

behavior: When users inspect `conan cache save` help, the `--file` option is described as accepting a generic output file rather than only a `.tgz` archive.
The `--file` help text explicitly lists `.tgz`, `.txz`, and `.tzst` as allowed extensions.
The help output marks `.txz` and `.tzst` as experimental formats.
The help output states that `.tzst` requires Python 3.14 or newer.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs help for `conan cache save`, the `--file` option should advertise `.tgz`, `.txz`, and `.tzst` as supported filename extensions.
When the user reads the `--file` help text, it should no longer imply that the command only saves to `.tgz` files.
When the user reviews the format information for `--file`, it should clearly indicate that `.txz` and `.tzst` are experimental.
When the user reviews the format information for `--file`, it should clearly indicate that `.tzst` depends on Python 3.14 or later.

task_19.title: Generate CMakeConfigDeps targets for requires-only components
task_19.description: Conan 2.26.0 fixes CMakeConfigDeps so that components with no direct libraries, include paths, frameworks, system libraries, or defines still produce a CMake target when they declare component requirements. This preserves dependency-only or aggregating components in generated CMake dependency metadata and keeps their transitive links available to consumers.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `CMakeConfigDeps` generates a component target when a package component exists only to require other components, so consumers can still resolve and link that component through generated CMake dependency files.

expectation.grounded: When Conan generates CMake dependency files with `CMakeConfigDeps`, a `cpp_info.components[...]` entry that is not an executable and declares `requires` must still result in a generated component target even if it has no own `includedirs`, `libs`, `frameworks`, `system_libs`, `package_framework`, or `defines`. The generated metadata must preserve the declared component requirements so consumers can link against the dependency-only component target and receive its transitive dependencies.
expectation.conceptual: Dependency-only components should remain visible in generated CMake package metadata. If a component exists purely as an aggregation or forwarding target for other components, consumers should still be able to reference it and obtain the expected transitive linkage.

constraints.grounded: This fix must not cause executable components to be emitted as library-style targets, and components that still have neither linkable metadata nor `requires` should remain omitted. Existing behavior for components with direct libraries or other package metadata must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: Only components that carry meaningful dependency relationships should gain new generated targets. The change should be additive for dependency-only components and should not alter unrelated component generation behavior.

behavior: A component that declares `requires` is treated as target-worthy by `CMakeConfigDeps` even when it contributes no direct libraries, include directories, frameworks, system libraries, package frameworks, or preprocessor definitions.
Generated CMake dependency metadata now includes a component target for dependency-only components instead of silently omitting them.
The generated target continues to expose the component's declared requirements so transitive component linkage is preserved for consumers.
Components marked as executables remain excluded from this target generation path.
acceptance_criteria: When a package component has only `requires` and no direct compile or link metadata, generating dependencies with `CMakeConfigDeps` should still produce a consumable CMake target for that component.
When a consumer links against that generated dependency-only component target, it should receive the component requirements declared by the package metadata.
When a component has neither its own metadata nor any declared requirements, `CMakeConfigDeps` should continue to omit it from generated targets.
When a component is an executable, this change should not cause it to be generated as a normal component library target.

task_21.title: Abstract the CMakeToolchain fallback toolchain-file tip
task_21.description: The upgrade refines the user-facing CMakeToolchain usage hint emitted for generated presets. For older CMake workflows, the displayed fallback command now refers to the toolchain file through a generic output-folder placeholder instead of a concrete generated path, while preserving the rest of the guidance and avoiding duplicate toolchain-file arguments when one is already provided.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the CMakeToolchain generator presents a portable fallback command for older CMake versions by abstracting the displayed toolchain-file location to an output-folder placeholder instead of a concrete generated path.

expectation.grounded: When CMakeToolchain emits its preset guidance for a consumer project, the informational hint for `cmake<3.23` should show `-DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE` using an abstract `<output_folder>/<toolchain_file>` form when no explicit `CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE` cache variable is already present. The hint should continue to include the selected generator and other cache variables, and the `cmake>=3.23` preset-based guidance should remain available.
expectation.conceptual: Users who rely on Conan's printed CMake invocation guidance should see a generic, reusable toolchain-file reference for older CMake versions rather than a concrete build-output path. The guidance should stay complete and should not repeat a toolchain-file argument if the user already defined one.

constraints.grounded: Only the emitted guidance text should change.
