Preset generation, toolchain file contents, preset names, generator selection, and cache-variable rendering semantics should remain unchanged, except that the fallback hint must not append an extra `-DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE` when `CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE` is already part of the cache variables.
constraints.conceptual: This is an informational compatibility fix, not a change to how builds are configured or generated. Existing explicit toolchain overrides and the rest of the printed CMake guidance should keep behaving the same way.

behavior: For consumer-facing CMakeToolchain guidance, the fallback command shown for CMake versions earlier than 3.23 should display the toolchain-file argument with an abstract `<output_folder>` placeholder instead of a concrete output path.
If `CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE` is already present in the cache variables supplied to the guidance, the fallback command should not add a second toolchain-file argument.
Other cache variables should continue to appear in the fallback command, with quoting preserved for values that contain spaces.
The preset-based guidance for CMake 3.23 and later should remain unchanged and be displayed alongside the fallback command.
acceptance_criteria: When CMakeToolchain reports preset usage for a consumer project, it should still present a `cmake --preset` command for CMake 3.23 and later.

When the same output includes a fallback command for CMake versions earlier than 3.23 and no explicit `CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE` cache variable was provided, it should show the toolchain file through an abstract `<output_folder>` placeholder rather than a concrete generated path.
When an explicit `CMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE` cache variable is already part of the configuration, the fallback command should include only that single toolchain-file definition.
When cache variable values contain spaces, the displayed fallback command should keep those values quoted so the guidance remains usable.

task_20.title: Fix MSBuildDeps build-context component transitives
task_20.description: Conan 2.26.0 fixes a bug in MSBuildDeps so transitive dependencies reached through components of build requirements are resolved in the correct build context. This prevents generated MSBuild property sheets for tool requirements from importing host-context dependency props and restores consistent dependency wiring for component-based build tools.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `MSBuildDeps` correctly resolves transitive dependencies referenced by components of build requirements, so generated MSBuild property sheets use the build-context dependency graph instead of host-context imports when tool requirements expose components.

expectation.grounded: When `conan.tools.microsoft.MSBuildDeps` generates props for a `tool_requires` package with components, transitive package and component dependencies reached from those components must be resolved with build-context-aware dependency naming. The generated dependency imports for those transitives should therefore target the build-context package or component props, while still tolerating transitives that were skipped from generation.
expectation.conceptual: `MSBuildDeps` should keep build-time dependencies internally consistent: if a tool requirement component depends on another build requirement or one of its components, the generated MSBuild props should continue following the build dependency graph all the way through.

constraints.grounded: Do not alter the existing resolution behavior for host-context dependencies or same-package component references. If a transitive dependency is not present in the generated dependency set, `MSBuildDeps` should continue omitting it instead of failing.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to correcting incorrect context selection for generated MSBuild dependency imports. Existing valid dependency wiring should remain stable, and missing or skipped transitive entries should not turn generation into an error.

behavior: `MSBuildDeps` now resolves transitive dependency names for build-context components using build-aware dependency naming instead of the raw package reference name.

If a component of a build requirement depends on a transitive component from another build requirement, the generated props import the build-context component/property sheet rather than the host-context equivalent.

If a component of a build requirement depends on the root package of another transitive build requirement, the generated props import the build-context package/property sheet rather than the host-context equivalent.
Transitive dependencies that were skipped from generation continue to be ignored without causing `MSBuildDeps` generation to fail.
acceptance_criteria: When `MSBuildDeps` is used with a `tool_requires` package whose components depend on components from another build requirement, the generated MSBuild props should reference the transitive dependency in build context, not the host-context props.
When a component of a build requirement depends on the overall package of another transitive build requirement, the generated props should import the build-context package props.
When the same generator is used for regular host requirements, existing host-context dependency naming should remain unchanged.
When a transitive dependency is skipped and therefore has no generated props, `MSBuildDeps` should still complete generation without raising an error.

task_22.title: Preserve CPS package preprocessor definitions across Conan import/export
task_22.description: The CPS integration now correctly carries package preprocessor definitions through Conan serialization and parsing. Definitions are represented in the CPS format with language-aware scopes, imported back into Conan as normal compile definitions, and merged with predictable precedence so packages no longer lose or misread defines during CPS-based consumption.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CPS package preprocessor definitions are parsed and preserved correctly when Conan exports package metadata to CPS and when Conan reads CPS metadata back into dependency information, including definitions with assigned values and definitions without values.

expectation.grounded: When converting Conan metadata to CPS via `CPSComponent.from_cpp_info`, `cpp_info.defines` must be serialized into the CPS `definitions` field as a language-keyed mapping using CPS language identifiers (`c`, `cpp`, or `*` when no language is declared). When converting CPS back to Conan via `CPS.to_conan`, component `definitions` must be flattened back into `CppInfo.defines` as standard define entries, preserving both bare defines and `NAME=value` definitions. If the same definition appears in multiple CPS language scopes, wildcard definitions must be applied first and overridden by `c` and then `cpp` definitions.
expectation.conceptual: Conan should reliably preserve compile definitions when exchanging package metadata through CPS files. Consumers should receive the same effective preprocessor definitions regardless of whether a package was described directly in Conan metadata or reconstructed from CPS metadata, and language-specific CPS definitions should override generic ones in a predictable way.

constraints.grounded: Packages with no preprocessor definitions must continue to behave as before and must not gain synthetic definitions. The fix must not change how includes, library locations, required components, link libraries, or link languages are interpreted beyond the definition-parsing correction. Definitions without an explicit value must remain observable as bare define entries rather than being discarded or converted into malformed assignments.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be limited to correcting preprocessor-definition handling. Existing package structure, dependency linkage, and library metadata should remain stable, and packages that do not use compile definitions should be unaffected.

behavior: CPS component definitions are no longer treated as a flat list; they are interpreted as language-scoped definition maps in the CPS representation.
Conan compile definitions exported to CPS are converted from string entries into keyed CPS definitions that preserve both simple defines and key-value defines.
When CPS metadata is imported, wildcard definitions are combined with language-specific definitions so that more specific language scopes override generic definitions.
The effective definitions exposed through Conan after CPS parsing are returned as standard compile-definition entries that downstream consumers can use normally.
Packages with one component or multiple components retain their component-level definitions during CPS-to-Conan conversion instead of dropping or misparsing them.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan package defines compile definitions in `cpp_info.defines` and is exported to CPS, the generated CPS metadata should contain those definitions in the public `definitions` field without losing names or assigned values.

When a CPS component defines compile definitions in wildcard and language-specific scopes, importing that CPS metadata into Conan should yield the effective compile definitions with language-specific values taking precedence over wildcard values.
When a CPS definition has no assigned value, importing it into Conan should expose it as a normal bare preprocessor define rather than omitting it or rewriting it as an invalid assignment.
When a package has no compile definitions, CPS import and export should continue to work without introducing definition-related output or regressions.
When Conan reconstructs dependency metadata from CPS for package components, component compile definitions should remain available to consumers alongside the existing include and linkage metadata.

task_24.title: Use hash terminology for checksum verification
task_24.description: The upgrade corrects user-facing checksum terminology so Conan refers to MD5, SHA-1, and SHA-256 values as hashes instead of signatures, including the mismatch errors surfaced when file verification fails.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that checksum verification features consistently describe MD5, SHA-1, and SHA-256 values as hashes rather than signatures, so users see accurate terminology in the API documentation and in checksum mismatch failures.

expectation.grounded: The public checksum helpers `check_md5`, `check_sha1`, and `check_sha256` should describe their expected values as hashes, and when verification fails they should still raise `ConanException` but report a hash mismatch, including the provided hash and the computed hash for the checked file.
expectation.conceptual: Checksum validation should use correct hashing terminology everywhere users interact with it. If a file's expected checksum does not match its actual checksum, the failure should clearly indicate that the hash check failed and show both the expected and actual hash values.

constraints.grounded: This change must preserve the existing checksum-validation flow and failure mechanism: the same checksum helper APIs remain available, mismatches still raise `ConanException`, and the change is limited to correcting user-visible terminology from signature to hash.
constraints.conceptual: The update should improve wording without changing how checksum verification works. Existing workflows should continue to validate files the same way, with only the user-visible language becoming more accurate.

behavior: Checksum helper documentation refers to MD5, SHA-1, and SHA-256 values as hashes instead of signatures.
A checksum mismatch continues to fail verification through `ConanException`.
Checksum mismatch errors describe the failure as a hash failure rather than a signature failure.
Checksum mismatch errors expose both the user-supplied hash value and the computed hash value for the file being checked.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer reads the public documentation for `check_md5`, `check_sha1`, or `check_sha256`, it should describe the expected checksum input as a hash.
When `check_md5` is given a file whose actual digest differs from the expected value, it should raise `ConanException` describing an MD5 hash mismatch.
When `check_sha1` is given a file whose actual digest differs from the expected value, it should raise `ConanException` describing a SHA-1 hash mismatch.
When `check_sha256` is given a file whose actual digest differs from the expected value, it should raise `ConanException` describing a SHA-256 hash mismatch.
When any of these checksum checks fail, the surfaced error should identify both the provided hash and the computed hash for the checked file.

task_23.title: Warn Conan users that Python 3.7 support is deprecated
task_23.description: Conan 2.26.0 adds a user-visible deprecation warning when the CLI runs on Python 3.7, reflecting that Python 3.7 is end-of-life and will no longer be supported in a future Conan release. The change is advisory and should not change normal command execution for supported runtimes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan informs users when they run the CLI on Python 3.7, because that interpreter version is deprecated and future Conan releases will remove support for it.

expectation.grounded: When the Conan CLI executes successfully under Python 3.7, it should emit a visible deprecation warning telling users that Python 3.7 is end-of-life and that future Conan versions will drop support for it. This warning should be advisory only, should not replace normal command output, and should not change the command's success result. Conan executions under Python versions other than 3.7 should not emit this Python 3.7 deprecation warning.
expectation.conceptual: Users running Conan on Python 3.7 should be clearly warned that their interpreter is deprecated and will stop being supported in a future release, while Conan continues to behave normally. Users on supported Python versions should not see this warning.

constraints.grounded: Do not fail, block, or otherwise change Conan command behavior solely because the interpreter is Python 3.7. Preserve existing command exit behavior and error handling. Limit the new deprecation notice to Python 3.7 runtime executions.
constraints.conceptual: The deprecation handling must remain informational only, must not disrupt normal CLI behavior, and must only appear for the deprecated interpreter version.

behavior: Successful Conan CLI runs on Python 3.7 display a deprecation warning about upcoming removal of Python 3.7 support.
The deprecation notice is emitted as a user-visible warning and does not convert a successful command into a failure.
Conan runs on Python versions other than 3.7 do not display the Python 3.7 deprecation warning.
Existing failure handling for CLI errors remains in place and is not replaced by the interpreter deprecation notice.
acceptance_criteria: When a user runs a Conan command with Python 3.7 and the command completes successfully, Conan should show a visible warning that Python 3.7 is end-of-life and that future Conan versions will drop support for it.
When the same Conan command is run with a Python version other than 3.7, Conan should not show the Python 3.7 deprecation warning.
When the warning is shown for a Python 3.7 run, the command should still finish with its normal successful outcome.
When a Conan command fails for its own reason, Conan should preserve its normal error and exit behavior without the deprecation handling changing that failure path.

task_27.title: Preserve version-like conf values as strings
task_27.description: Conan 2.26.0 fixes configuration parsing for built-in version-like settings so numeric-looking values are preserved as strings instead of being coerced and losing formatting such as trailing zeroes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that built-in configuration values that represent version or update identifiers are preserved exactly as user-provided strings so numeric-like inputs do not lose trailing zeroes or other formatting during configuration parsing.

expectation.grounded: When Conan loads built-in conf entries `tools.microsoft:msvc_update` and `core:required_conan_version`, it should parse their values as strings rather than evaluating them as numeric literals. Numeric-looking inputs for these keys must preserve the exact textual value after trimming surrounding whitespace, and downstream behavior that consumes these conf values should observe the unchanged string form.
expectation.conceptual: Version-like configuration settings should keep the exact value the user typed, even if the value looks like a number. This prevents configuration-driven behavior from changing because the parser normalized or truncated part of the value.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the existing parsing behavior for other conf keys that still support evaluated numbers, booleans, and collection-like values. The forced string treatment should apply only to the designated built-in conf entries that require exact textual preservation.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be narrowly scoped to settings whose value format must remain literal, while ordinary configuration values should continue behaving as they did before the upgrade.

behavior: `tools.microsoft:msvc_update` is parsed and stored as a string during conf loading.
Numeric-like `tools.microsoft:msvc_update` values keep trailing zeroes and other literal formatting instead of being converted to a float-like value.
`core:required_conan_version` is also treated as a string-preserved built-in conf value.
Other conf entries continue using the existing general parsing behavior for non-string literal types.
acceptance_criteria: When a user sets `tools.microsoft:msvc_update` to a dotted numeric-like value that includes trailing zeroes, Conan should preserve the exact text of that value and use it unchanged in observable MSVC configuration behavior.
When a user sets `core:required_conan_version` to a version-like value, Conan should retain it as a string rather than coercing it to a numeric type.
When users provide surrounding whitespace for these built-in string-preserved conf values, Conan should ignore the outer whitespace while keeping the intended value text intact.
When users configure other unrelated conf keys with numeric, boolean, or collection values, Conan should continue to parse those values with the pre-existing semantics.

task_26.title: Fix context-only graph listing for unnamed consumer recipes
task_26.description: Conan 2.26.0 fixes a `conan list` graph-filtering bug so `--graph-context=build-only` and `--graph-context=host-only` work correctly for graphs rooted at unnamed consumer recipes. Context-only filtering now ignores non-package graph nodes and only evaluates real referenced package binaries when deciding whether a package belongs exclusively to the build or host context.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `conan list` can process dependency graphs generated from consumer recipes without a name when `--graph-context=build-only` or `--graph-context=host-only` is used, and that context-only results are calculated only from actual package entries.

expectation.grounded: When `conan list` is run with `--graph=<graph>` and `--graph-context=build-only` or `--graph-context=host-only`, it should compute context exclusivity only from graph nodes that have a valid package reference and `package_id`, excluding consumer recipe nodes and virtual recipe nodes. The command should complete successfully for graphs rooted at unnamed consumer recipes, and a package identified by its reference plus package ID should only appear in a context-only result when it exists exclusively in the requested context.
expectation.conceptual: Context-only graph listing should ignore synthetic root or virtual nodes and consider only real packages. Users should be able to run build-only or host-only listing against graphs from unnamed consumer recipes without failures and without seeing packages that are shared across both contexts.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing graph listing behavior for nodes that already provide both a package reference and `package_id`. Do not alter the meaning of `build-only` or `host-only`: packages present in both build and host contexts must remain excluded from both context-only outputs.
constraints.conceptual: Keep normal package listing behavior unchanged for real dependencies. The fix should only make context-only filtering robust and accurate by preventing non-package nodes from affecting the result.

behavior: `conan list --graph-context=build-only` and `--graph-context=host-only` ignore consumer recipe nodes when deriving context-only package results.
Virtual recipe nodes are excluded from context-only package grouping.
Graph nodes that do not provide both a package reference and a package ID do not participate in context exclusivity calculations.
Context-only inclusion is determined per package reference and package ID pair, so packages present in both build and host contexts are not listed as build-only or host-only.
Graphs rooted at unnamed consumer recipes can be listed with context-only filters without the command failing.
acceptance_criteria: Given a dependency graph produced from a consumer recipe without a name, when `conan list --graph=<graph> --graph-context=build-only` is executed, it should complete successfully and only show packages that appear exclusively in the build context.

Given a dependency graph produced from a consumer recipe without a name, when `conan list --graph=<graph> --graph-context=host-only` is executed, it should complete successfully and only show packages that appear exclusively in the host context.
When the same resolved package binary appears in both build and host contexts in the graph, it should not appear in either context-only result.

When the graph includes consumer or virtual nodes without a real package reference, those nodes should not be listed as package results and should not affect whether another package is considered build-only or host-only.

task_25.title: Honor CMake filename variants for packaged config discovery
task_25.description: Conan 2.26.0 fixes `CMakeConfigDeps` so dependencies that declare `cmake_file_name_variants` remain discoverable through those supported names even when the package ships its own CMake config files. Generated CMake dependency path entries now stay aligned across the primary package name and its supported variants, preventing missed package resolution during consumption.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `CMakeConfigDeps` honors declared `cmake_file_name_variants` when exposing package discovery paths, including packages that ship their own CMake config files, so consumers can locate the same dependency through any supported variant name.

expectation.grounded: When a dependency uses `CMakeConfigDeps` and defines `cmake_file_name_variants`, the generator should recognize in-package `<name>-config.cmake` and `<name>Config.cmake` files for any supported variant name and expose the corresponding package directory through the generated CMake package directory variables for every supported name. When discovery falls back to Conan-generated dependency files, the generator should likewise publish the generated directory for every supported variant rather than only the primary `cmake_file_name`.
expectation.conceptual: Packages that intentionally support multiple CMake file-name variants should behave the same regardless of which supported variant a consumer uses. If the package ships its own CMake config files, those files should still be found through the declared variants; if Conan generates the config files, the generated package directory should also be available through those same variants.

constraints.grounded: The change should stay scoped to `CMakeConfigDeps` package-path exposure and preserve support for both `-config.cmake` and `Config.cmake` naming styles. Repeated package folders should not be duplicated in the generator's multi-path directory tracking for a supported name. Existing behavior for the primary package name must remain intact.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should expand supported discovery aliases without changing what package is resolved or disrupting the default CMake naming flow. Supported variants should map to the same package location consistently and without duplicate search entries.

behavior: `CMakeConfigDeps` treats declared `cmake_file_name_variants` as valid names when scanning a package folder for shipped CMake config files.
If any supported variant has a matching shipped `-config.cmake` or `Config.cmake` file, the generated CMake package directory variables point all supported names to that package folder.
The multi-value package directory tracking used by the generator is populated for each supported variant name while avoiding duplicate folder entries for the same name.
When Conan uses the generated dependency config directory instead of a shipped in-package config file, all supported variant names resolve to the generated directory instead of only the primary name.
acceptance_criteria: When a package declares `cmake_file_name_variants` and ships a matching in-package CMake config file for one of those supported names, installing `CMakeConfigDeps` should make the dependency discoverable through every supported variant name.

When a package declares `cmake_file_name_variants` and Conan generates the dependency config files itself, the generated CMake package directory variables should be emitted for every supported variant name.
When both single-path and multi-path package directory variables are produced, each supported variant name should resolve to the same package folder without duplicate directory entries.
When a consumer uses the primary package name, dependency discovery should continue to work as before.

task_29.title: Correct CMakeToolchain variable escaping for CMake syntax
task_29.description: The upgrade fixes how Conan emits `CMakeToolchain.variables` into generated CMake toolchain files. String values containing CMake-sensitive characters are now escaped correctly for both regular and configuration-specific variables, while already escaped content is preserved instead of being escaped again.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan 2.26.0 generates valid CMake toolchain variable definitions when `CMakeToolchain.variables` contains string values with backslashes, double quotes, or dollar signs, including configuration-specific variables, without corrupting values that are already escaped.

expectation.grounded: When `CMakeToolchain.variables` and `CMakeToolchain.variables.<configuration>` are rendered into the generated CMake toolchain, string values must be passed through Conan's CMake escaping logic before emission. The escaping behavior must cover backslashes, double quotes, and dollar signs in CMake string values, and it must avoid re-escaping character pairs that are already escaped. Non-string variable values must continue to be emitted without string escaping changes.
expectation.conceptual: Projects that define toolchain variables with Windows-style paths, quoted text, or dollar-prefixed content should get usable CMake definitions after upgrade. The generated toolchain should preserve the intended value semantics for normal and per-configuration variables, and repeated processing should not progressively alter already escaped values.

constraints.grounded: The fix applies to generated output for `CMakeToolchain.variables` and configuration-specific variable entries only. It must preserve current handling for non-string values and must not introduce duplicate escaping for existing escaped sequences involving backslash, double quote, or dollar sign.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be limited to making generated CMake variable values syntactically correct and stable. Existing valid non-string values should behave as before, and upgrading should not unexpectedly rewrite values that were already properly escaped.

behavior: String values assigned through `CMakeToolchain.variables` are escaped for CMake syntax before being written to generated toolchain definitions.
Configuration-specific entries under `CMakeToolchain.variables.<configuration>` receive the same escaping treatment as global toolchain variables.
Backslashes, double quotes, and dollar signs in unescaped string values are emitted in a CMake-safe form.
Existing escaped pairs for backslash, double quote, or dollar sign are preserved rather than escaped a second time.
Non-string variable values are left unchanged by the CMake escaping helper.
acceptance_criteria: When a consumer sets a `CMakeToolchain.variables` string value containing a Windows path, the generated CMake toolchain should preserve the path content in valid CMake syntax.

When a consumer sets a `CMakeToolchain.variables` string value containing double quotes or dollar signs, the generated CMake toolchain should emit a value that CMake can parse without changing the intended content.

When configuration-specific variables are defined through `CMakeToolchain.variables.<configuration>`, their generated definitions should follow the same escaping rules as non-configuration-specific variables.
When a string value already contains valid escaping for backslashes, double quotes, or dollar signs, generation should not add another escaping layer that changes the resulting value.
When a toolchain variable value is not a string, generation should continue to handle it without applying string escaping behavior.

task_30.title: Fix cpp_info type serialization round-trip
task_30.description: The upgrade fixes Conan 2.26.0 serialization and deserialization for `cpp_info` entries that use the `type` field, so saved metadata preserves the declared package or component type and can be loaded back without losing meaning or corrupting state.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `cpp_info` metadata using the `type` field can be serialized and deserialized correctly, preserving declared package and component types and safely handling unset types during persistence and reload.

expectation.grounded: When `cpp_info.type` is set on package-level or component-level metadata, serialization should emit its public string form instead of a raw internal object. When serialized `cpp_info` data is deserialized, fields that have public attribute setters, including `type`, should be restored through those attributes so the loaded object preserves the expected `cpp_info` semantics. Unset `type` values should remain absent/null rather than being converted to an invalid value.
expectation.conceptual: Persisted `cpp_info` data should round-trip cleanly when a package or component declares a type. Saving and loading the metadata should preserve the visible type information, and components without a type should stay unset.

constraints.grounded: The fix should not change the serialized shape of unrelated `cpp_info` fields such as requirements, properties, locations, languages, executables, or collections. Deserialization must continue to restore fields that do not expose public setters, while using public setters where available. Null `type` values must remain supported for components.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be limited to correcting persistence behavior for typed `cpp_info` data without regressing other metadata fields or forcing type information where none was provided.

behavior: Serializing `cpp_info` with a declared `type` now stores the type as its public string representation.
Deserializing serialized `cpp_info` data now restores fields through public attributes when available, so `type` is reconstructed with normal attribute semantics instead of bypassing them.
Component entries whose `type` is unset continue to serialize as null/absent-equivalent values and remain unset after reload.
Property-style fields that do not expose direct setters continue to deserialize successfully.
acceptance_criteria: When a package `cpp_info` declares a `type` and its metadata is saved, the persisted form should contain the expected string value for that type.
When serialized `cpp_info` metadata containing a package or component `type` is loaded back, the resulting `cpp_info` object should expose the same declared type to consumers.
When a component has no `type`, saving and loading its `cpp_info` should keep that component type unset rather than assigning an unintended value.
When `cpp_info` metadata includes both `type` and other standard metadata fields, the data should remain loadable without breaking those other fields.

task_28.title: Avoid redundant rebuilds for existing compatible binaries
task_28.description: The Conan 2.26.0 upgrade changes compatible binary resolution so `--build=compatible` does not rebuild a package when a suitable compatible binary already exists in the cache or can be resolved from remotes. It also reuses prior resolution for repeated package references in the dependency graph, preventing duplicate processing and unnecessary builds.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that using `--build=compatible` does not rebuild a package when an already compatible binary exists. Ensure that repeated resolution of the same package reference reuses the existing binary decision instead of triggering duplicate compatible-build work.

expectation.grounded: When Conan resolves a package with `--build=compatible`, it must first search compatible package IDs among already available binaries in the local cache and configured remotes before deciding to build a compatible binary. If the originally requested package configuration is invalid but a compatible binary exists, Conan should still resolve to that compatible binary and expose the corresponding runtime outcome such as cache use, download, or update instead of forcing a rebuild. Repeated evaluations of the same package reference within the graph should reuse the previously resolved binary state rather than reprocessing it.
expectation.conceptual: Compatible-build mode should prefer reuse over rebuild. If a suitable compatible package is already available, the package manager should consume that existing artifact and keep graph resolution stable, only building a compatible package when no existing compatible binary can satisfy the request.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress normal cache and remote revision selection: if a compatible binary already exists in cache, it should resolve as cache unless a newer remote revision requires update handling. Preserve the ability to build a compatible binary when no existing compatible package is found. Do not perform duplicate binary evaluation or duplicate build scheduling for repeated identical package references in the same dependency graph.
constraints.conceptual: The change should only eliminate unnecessary rebuilds. Existing behavior for selecting cached versus newer remote artifacts should remain intact, and compatible builds should still occur when reuse is not possible.

behavior: Conan now checks whether a package reference has already been resolved earlier in the graph before re-evaluating that node, and reuses the cached resolution for duplicates.
In `--build=compatible` flows, Conan searches for existing compatible binaries before considering a compatible rebuild.
Compatible binary lookup is allowed to succeed even when the originally requested configuration is invalid, as long as a compatible package ID resolves to an existing binary.
When a compatible binary exists in cache and remote comparison does not require an update, Conan resolves to the cached revision instead of leaving the node unresolved for rebuild.
A compatible build is only selected after existing compatible binaries have been checked and none of them satisfy the request.
acceptance_criteria: When `create` or `install` is run with `--build=compatible` and a suitable compatible binary already exists in the local cache, it should use that binary and should not rebuild the package.

When `create` or `install` is run with `--build=compatible` and a suitable compatible binary exists on a configured remote, it should resolve that remote artifact through the normal download or update path before deciding to build.

When the requested package configuration is invalid for direct use but a compatible binary exists, the command should resolve to the compatible binary rather than rebuilding solely because the requested package ID was invalid.

When the same package reference is evaluated more than once within a dependency graph, Conan should reuse the earlier binary resolution and should not schedule an extra compatible build for the duplicate evaluation.
When no suitable compatible binary exists in cache or remotes and compatible build mode applies, Conan should still build an allowed compatible binary.

task_31.title: Preserve CPS component CMake target naming and metadata
task_31.description: Conan 2.26.0 fixes CPS-to-Conan conversion so CPS packages, especially those with a single component, expose the expected CMake package and target names while preserving component definitions, requirements, system libraries, and library location metadata.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that CPS-derived package metadata preserves expected CMake package and component target naming, including for single-component CPS packages, and retains the component's compile definitions, dependencies, system libraries, and default component mapping during Conan consumption.

expectation.grounded: When `CPS.load(...).to_conan()` converts CPS metadata into `CppInfo`, it should preserve `default_components`, keep component include directories, requirements, system libraries, library and binary locations, and set CMake-facing properties so the package is identified by its CPS name through `cmake_file_name` and each exposed target follows `cmake_target_name=<package-name>::<component-name>`, including when the CPS package has only one component. CPS `definitions` should be translated into Conan `defines` by combining generic (`*`) and language-specific (`c`, `cpp`) entries, with specific entries overriding generic ones and valueless definitions remaining valid defines.
expectation.conceptual: Loading package metadata from CPS should yield Conan/CMake integration that matches the CPS package name and component names. Consumers should be able to discover the package by its CPS name and link the expected component-qualified target, while compile definitions and dependency metadata remain intact for both single-component and multi-component packages.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress multi-component CPS conversion: component-scoped `requires`, `system_libs`, include directories, and library or bindir metadata must remain attached to the correct component. The naming fix must not drop single-component dependencies or flatten away the component-qualified CMake target. Definition conversion must preserve both bare defines and key/value defines and respect language-specific override precedence over generic definitions.
constraints.conceptual: Correct the exposed naming and metadata preservation without changing unrelated package discovery behavior or losing component boundaries. The upgrade should maintain existing component semantics while making single-component CPS packages behave consistently with the documented target naming pattern.

behavior: `CPS.load(...).to_conan()` now carries `default_components` into the generated Conan `CppInfo`.

A CPS package with one component is converted with CMake package metadata based on the CPS package name and an exposed target name in the form `<package>::<component>` instead of being treated as an unnamed flat target.
Component `requires` and `system_libs` are propagated consistently for both single-component and multi-component CPS packages.
CPS compile definitions are converted from language-scoped definition maps into Conan `defines` by aggregating generic, C, and C++ definitions with language-specific values overriding generic ones.
When a component declares library paths through its CPS location fields, the resulting Conan metadata keeps the resolved library information and binary directory on that same component.
acceptance_criteria: When a CPS package named `X` exposes a component `Y`, Conan-generated CMake metadata should identify the package using `X` and expose a consumable target named `X::Y`, even if `Y` is the package's only component.
When a single-component CPS package declares component dependencies, those requirements should remain visible in the converted Conan metadata and participate in downstream consumption.

When CPS definitions include generic entries plus C- or C++-specific entries, the converted Conan defines should include the merged result, preserve flag-style defines, and prefer the language-specific value when the same key appears in both places.

When a CPS component declares system libraries or explicit library and binary locations, the converted Conan metadata should retain those values on the correct component without changing multi-component behavior.

task_32.title: Prevent [buildenv] pattern leakage across packages
task_32.description: Conan 2.26.0 fixes a build environment isolation bug so per-package [buildenv] entries no longer corrupt or leak into other packages when environments are copied and composed across multiple dependencies.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that per-package [buildenv] definitions are isolated per package when multiple packages are processed, so package-specific build environment values do not corrupt or leak into other packages' build environments.

expectation.grounded: When Conan composes build environments from profile [buildenv] entries that include per-package patterns, copied conan.tools.env.environment.Environment instances must keep independent variable state. Applying package-specific environment changes to one package must not mutate the source Environment or sibling copies, and only matching packages should observe those additional environment values.
expectation.conceptual: Build environment configuration should be evaluated independently for each package. Shared baseline environment settings may apply broadly, but package-specific additions must only affect the packages they target and must not alter the environment seen by other packages.

constraints.grounded: Preserve existing Environment copy behavior for defined, appended, prepended, unset, and path-based variables while preventing cross-copy mutation of environment entries. The fix must not change which [buildenv] entries match a package; it only prevents copied environment state from being shared across packages.
constraints.conceptual: Keep current environment features and matching rules intact while eliminating state leakage between packages. The change should improve isolation, not redefine how environment variables are declared or matched.

behavior: Environment.copy() produces a new environment whose per-variable entries are copied rather than shared by reference.
Subsequent mutations to environment variables in one copied environment do not retroactively alter another copied environment or the original source environment.

When [buildenv] contains both global entries and per-package pattern entries, package-specific values are composed only into the matching package's build environment and do not appear in unrelated packages.
acceptance_criteria: When a profile defines a global [buildenv] value and an additional value scoped to one package pattern, the targeted package should receive the global value plus its own scoped value.
When another package in the same installation does not match that per-package pattern, it should receive only the global [buildenv] value and no values intended for other packages.

When Conan copies an Environment during build environment composition, later changes made for one package should not change the environment content later observed for other packages derived from the same source.

task_33.title: Default platform revision for lockable platform requirements
task_33.description: Conan now gives platform-resolved dependencies a default `#platform` revision when `platform_requires` or `platform_tool_requires` does not provide one. This makes platform dependencies distinguishable in graph outputs and lockfiles, while still supporting explicit platform revisions when users need system changes to produce a different dependency identity.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dependencies resolved through `platform_requires` and `platform_tool_requires` get a stable revision identity by default so platform-provided dependencies can be locked, distinguished from regular package references, and optionally overridden with an explicit revision.

expectation.grounded: When `platform_requires` or `platform_tool_requires` resolves a dependency as a platform node and the resolved reference has no revision, the public reference should use revision `platform`. That revisioned reference should be the observable identity used in graph resolution outputs and lockfiles. If the resolved platform reference already has a revision, that revision should remain the resolved identity, and users should still be able to specify a different platform revision when they need to reflect system-level changes.
expectation.conceptual: Platform dependencies should no longer behave like revisionless references. By default they should resolve as a distinct `platform` revision so lockfiles can capture and replay them consistently, while still allowing users to choose a different revision when the underlying system dependency meaningfully changes.

constraints.grounded: Only platform-resolved `platform_requires` and `platform_tool_requires` references should receive the default `platform` revision. Name/version matching and revision compatibility for already-revisioned platform references must continue to apply, and non-platform dependency resolution behavior must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: The change should be limited to the identity of platform dependencies. Regular dependency resolution should keep working as before, and explicitly revisioned platform dependencies should not lose their intended identity.

behavior: A platform-resolved requirement with no revision is normalized to revision `platform` instead of remaining revisionless.
The same default platform revision behavior applies to both `platform_requires` and `platform_tool_requires`.

Platform dependency identities exposed through graph resolution and lockfiles now include a revision, allowing platform entries to be recorded and matched distinctly from normal cached package references.
If a resolved platform dependency already carries a revision, that revision is propagated as the resolved platform identity instead of replacing it with an empty revision.
acceptance_criteria: When a dependency declared via `platform_requires` resolves as a platform dependency without an explicit revision, it should appear as the same name and version with revision `#platform`.
When a dependency declared via `platform_tool_requires` resolves as a platform dependency without an explicit revision, it should appear as the same name and version with revision `#platform`.

When a lockfile is created from a graph containing such platform dependencies, it should record those dependencies using their revisioned platform identity so later resolution under the same platform configuration can match them.
When a platform dependency already resolves with a non-empty revision, it should keep that revision as its observable identity instead of becoming revisionless.

task_34.title: Add riscv64 support to apt and yum system package mapping
task_34.description: Conan 2.26.0 fixes a missing architecture mapping so Linux system package installation through apt and yum works correctly for riscv64 targets. This removes a gap that could block recipes relying on system requirements on riscv64 environments.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that Conan system package installation supports `arch=riscv64` for Linux environments that use `apt` or `yum`, so recipes can resolve and install architecture-qualified system dependencies correctly.

expectation.grounded: When `conan.tools.system.package_manager.Apt` or `conan.tools.system.package_manager.Yum` operates with the default architecture mappings and the Conan architecture is `riscv64`, it should recognize that architecture and map it to the distro package architecture `riscv64`. `Apt` should continue using its existing architecture-qualified package naming convention, and `Yum` should continue using its own, with the new mapping applied for `riscv64`.
expectation.conceptual: Users targeting riscv64 Linux systems should be able to install system dependencies through Conan with apt- or yum-based package managers without the architecture being treated as unsupported or translated to an incorrect package architecture.

constraints.grounded: The change must be limited to the missing default `riscv64` mapping in `Apt` and `Yum`. Existing default mappings for other architectures must remain unchanged, and any caller-provided `arch_names` override must continue to take precedence over the built-in defaults.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should add riscv64 compatibility without changing behavior for other architectures or overriding explicit user customizations.

behavior: `Apt` recognizes Conan `arch=riscv64` and resolves the package architecture suffix as `riscv64`.
`Yum` recognizes Conan `arch=riscv64` and resolves the package architecture suffix as `riscv64`.
When Conan installs architecture-qualified system packages through apt on a riscv64 profile, package names are formed with the correct riscv64 architecture qualifier.
When Conan installs architecture-qualified system packages through yum on a riscv64 profile, package names are formed with the correct riscv64 architecture qualifier.
acceptance_criteria: When a Conan workflow uses `Apt` with `arch=riscv64`, it should resolve architecture-qualified system package references using the distro architecture `riscv64`.
When a Conan workflow uses `Yum` with `arch=riscv64`, it should resolve architecture-qualified system package references using the distro architecture `riscv64`.
When the target architecture is any previously supported default architecture, apt and yum package resolution should behave the same as before.
When a consumer supplies a custom architecture mapping override to `Apt` or `Yum`, that override should still determine the resolved package architecture instead of the built-in defaults.
